paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: a message is only worth trusting if it comes from the LORD. In this passage, the LORD says the prophets of Jerusalem speak "visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD." (Jeremiah 23:16) And look at what He says about them: "I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message; I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied." (Jeremiah 23:21) Running fast and sounding sure doesn't make a word true.

Now, why would anybody listen to them? Because the message felt good. They kept telling people, "No harm will come to you." (Jeremiah 23:17) I think that's the part that should make us stop. A comfortable word can be a dangerous one when the LORD hasn't said it, and the LORD says these prophets "strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness." (Jeremiah 23:14)

So what do you do with that? You do what the LORD asks: "Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you." (Jeremiah 23:16) The LORD says that if these prophets had stood in His council, they would have proclaimed His words and turned His people back from their evil ways. (Jeremiah 23:22) Measure every word you hear by what God has actually said, and that's why we bake with the Word, friend. And the LORD isn't done talking about these prophets, so stay close.
